explainBack.question: Why do the lower Sol and Luna prices not reduce what a ChatGPT Plus subscriber pays each month?
explainBack.answer: Because those figures are per-token API prices: they meter text that developer software sends to the model over a separate connection, so cost scales with usage there. A ChatGPT subscription is a flat plan on a different product surface, and which models appear in that surface depends on plan and workspace settings, not on API price lists.
explainBack.expectedEvidence: The article must define the API as a developer channel paying for text processed, state the figures are not a subscription price, and tie account availability to plan/workspace settings.
explainBack.assessment: P003 supplies the API definition and billing boundary, P005 the plan/workspace availability rule, and P010 the usage-meter framing; the causal answer is fully supported in ordinary language.

unseenTransfer.scenario: A colleague on the free ChatGPT tier reads a headline that Sol costs 40% less and tells her team their plan is about to get cheaper and that Sol will appear in her chat app tomorrow.
unseenTransfer.question: Using the article's mechanism, what should she actually conclude and check?
unseenTransfer.answer: The percentage refers to per-token API pricing for developer usage, so no subscription or free tier changes price. Whether Sol appears for her depends on which service she uses and her plan/workspace settings under a gradual rollout, so she should open her own service's model picker rather than trust the announcement.
unseenTransfer.expectedEvidence: The reader would need the API-vs-subscription billing boundary (P003), the plan/workspace availability rule with gradual rollout (P005), and the check-your-own-picker procedure (P007).
unseenTransfer.assessment: All three elements are explicitly taught, so the mechanism transfers to this genuinely new situation without extra information.
